key_insight: Leverage the representational capacity of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to produce compact, cross-modal subject embeddings that condition diffusion-based image generation, enabling stronger identity preservation while improving instruction following and reducing copy‑paste artifacts.
problem_solved: Existing subject-driven generation pipelines treat text and reference images separately, which limits cross-modal reasoning and leads to weak identity preservation and copy‑paste artifacts when synthesizing new images of a subject under textual instructions.
method: Extract subject-aware, compact embeddings from a pretrained multimodal LLM (rather than separate image-only encoders) to capture joint visual-text semantics.
Condition a diffusion model on these MLLM-derived representations via lightweight adapters/prompting so generation respects both identity and instructions.
Train with identity-aware losses (e.g., reconstruction/contrastive constraints) and instruction alignment objectives to balance fidelity to the subject and compliance with text.
impact: Provides a practical way to squeeze extra cross-modal reasoning capacity from MLLMs to improve subject fidelity in generative pipelines without heavy retraining of large diffusion models; useful for avatars, personalized content, and controlled image editing.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: MLLM encodes reference(s) + text → compact subject embedding → conditioned diffusion model → output image
Before/after gallery: side-by-side comparisons showing reduced copy-paste artifacts and better identity preservation
Attention/conditioning visualization: heatmaps showing how MLLM embedding guides generation across diffusion timesteps
Ablation chart: bar plots comparing identity metrics and instruction-following scores across baseline vs. proposed conditioning strategies
paper_title: Squeezing Capacity from Multimodal Large Language Models for Subject-driven Generation
paper_authors: Shuhong Zheng, Aashish Kumar Misraa, Yu-Teng Li, Yu-Jhe Li, Igor Gilitschenski
